title: Ang 751–761: Suhi ashtpadis
tomorrow: what if you feel too clumsy to love well?

segments.voice: Yesterday, ang 749: whose head the Master is over, how could they suffer? Read as protection, and as a mind held steady. Guarded. Today, color.

One new red shirt goes in with the whites, and everything comes out pink. Some dyes run; some hold. Guru Nanak knew his dyes. On ang 751, where Suhi's longer hymns begin, he says, in paraphrase: the color of kasumbh, safflower, is raw; it lasts only a few days. So which color holds?
screen: `ONE RED SHIRT, A PINK LOAD.` → `SAFFLOWER: A RAW COLOR.` → `WHICH COLOR HOLDS?`

segments.voice: These are ashtpadis, longer hymns, and their singer is the soul-bride. In Gurbani the soul, whoever it belongs to, is pictured as a bride, and God as the husband she longs for. Safflower gave a bright red-orange that didn't last. Guru Nanak goes on, in paraphrase: without the Name, the bride wanders in doubt, robbed by the cheat of falsehood; but those dyed in the True One aren't born again. Listen to how physical it is. A bride's clothes, a bright dye, the color washing out in a few days. The bride who chases the quick color loses it. The color that holds is the one soaked in deep: love for the True One, the Name, the habit of remembering. Somewhere this week there's a wedding outfit on a hanger, bright and beautiful. The hymn doesn't sneer at it. It just says the dye on the cloth isn't the color that lasts. And the bride in these hymns isn't only a woman, and isn't only at a wedding. She's anyone who wants to belong to the One, and is learning which colors run. The bride.
screen: `THE SOUL IS THE BRIDE.` · `SAFFLOWER FADES IN DAYS.` · `DYED IN THE TRUE ONE, IT HOLDS.` · `NOT ONLY A WOMAN, NOT ONLY A WEDDING.` · then, large: `THE BRIDE.`

segments.voice: Hold or look at a piece of colored cloth near you: a scarf, a sleeve, a cushion. Look at the color for the sit, and notice where it's still bright and where it has already faded. Then let your eyes rest, and the breath with them.
Ang 751. Where Suhi's longer hymns begin, the soul-bride's ashtpadis, with safflower's quick color.
The bride: the soul, learning which colors run and which one holds. Day fifteen thirty-seven, colorfast.

notes: 2026-10-15 v3 written: shape senses (color and dye carry the idea; the practice is looking at colored cloth). Simran arc: Navi's wedding outfit bleeds dye three days before the wedding.
Confirm 'kachaa rang kasumbh kaa thoriaa din chaar jeeo' opens a Suhi ashtpadi on ang 751, and the paraphrase of the following lines. 'Din chaar' (four days) rendered 'a few days', as the idiom.
'Safflower gave a bright red-orange that didn't last' is a description of the dye; confirm wording.
The soul-bride as the soul (and God as husband) is the common Sikh reading; confirm phrasing 'whoever it belongs to'.
Outline practice says read ang 752; the voice keeps the practice physical (senses day). The Keeper may wish to add 'read ang 752' to howItsDone.
